speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry has been able to track the effectiveness of ScamShield in preventing scams since it was launched; (b) what percentage of the local population has downloaded this mobile application; and (c) whether the Ministry intends to introduce ScamShield or similar measures to identify and block scammers from using social media, e-commerce platforms and messaging mobile applications like WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram to trick victims.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the public adoption rate of ScamShield since its launch; (b) what is the Ministry’s assessment of the effectiveness of ScamShield; and (c) whether ScamShield complements malware detection apps used by banking customers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The iOS and Android versions of the ScamShield mobile app were launched in November 2020 and September 2022 respectively.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We do not track the number of unique users.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A user may download the ScamShield app on multiple devices.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ScamShield has been effective in protecting users from scam calls and SMSes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On top of phone calls blocked by ScamShield, the Police work closely with telecommunication companies (telcos) to block mobile lines suspected to be involved in scams.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the first half of 2023, more than 3,700 mobile lines which were believed to be used in scams were flagged by the Police for termination.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In addition, telcos blocked about 180 million suspected scam calls at the network level during this period.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) team is making enhancements to the ScamShield app so that users can more easily report scams.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is also working to improve the accuracy of scam SMS detections and to help users more easily set up the correct permission settings.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about measures to identify and block scammers from using social media, e-commerce platforms and messaging mobile applications.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: While ScamShield is not designed to block scammers on these platforms, it serves as an additional layer of defence and has a reporting function that allows users to alert the authorities about the scam calls and messages they receive.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It also complements the Government’s efforts to combat scams.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, the Police, upon detecting or receiving reports from the public on scammers who are using social media, e-commerce or messaging apps, will ask the platform operators to remove these accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the first half of 2023, more than 10,000 WhatsApp lines and 1,500 online monikers and advertisements that were believed to be used in scams were flagged out by the Police for termination.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Specifically, it provides the Police powers to direct online services to prevent suspected scam accounts or content from interacting with or reaching Singapore users.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Police can also require designated online services to implement systems, processes or measures to counter scams, such as requiring the verification of user identities against Government-issued identification documents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked whether ScamShield complements the malware detection apps used by banking customers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Major retail banks have introduced anti-malware security features on their banking apps, which seek to protect banking customers by detecting the presence of malware on their devices, and triggering actions such as blocking access to the banking app.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: While ScamShield is not designed to detect or block malware, it complements the anti-malware security features on banking apps by protecting users from other attack vectors, namely scam calls and scam SMSes, hence, further mitigating the risk of users falling prey to scams.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, to encourage usage of ScamShield, would the Ministry consider working with the Ministry of Communications and Information and have the app pre-loaded on all new handphones?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If the app is pre-loaded on new handphones, it would be easier for us to roll out educational campaigns to encourage all to use ScamShield, especially for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, I understand that the Minister of State has shared that for scammers using social media, e-commerce and messaging applications such as WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, the Ministry of Home Affairs actually works with the developers to remove these accounts from these platforms.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: So, my question is, are they given a timeline as to how fast they are supposed to remove such scam accounts?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, even if we were to pre-load the app, if the user does not know how to execute the permission settings, ScamShield will not be able to work effectively.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the second question, we work with the app developers as well as the platforms whenever we are informed about scams that are being perpetuated on social media platforms as well as other messaging applications.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There is no fixed timeline in place, but we require the operators to remove the content as soon as possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Sometimes, some of these platforms tell us that they require some time to investigate to make sure that on their end, it adheres to their community standards or that truly, they have conducted their investigations and that, it is, indeed, potentially a scam, and they would then need to go through their processes to remove the advertisement or the otherwise potential scam message.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, because of these factors, there is no specific timeline that the Police has set out, but depending on the likely harm and impact, the Police would do what is within their powers to encourage the platforms to remove those scam messages as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State to share if there are plans to upgrade ScamShield protection to cover other channels like emails, WhatsApp messages and, perhaps, malware, which the Minister of State said do not help in protection so far?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: The reason is, Mr Speaker, the Police have reported that we have already seen losses of $660 million last year and $330 million in the first half of the year.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Apart from these losses are the emotional stress on victims.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We should see the use of ScamShield vis-à-vis all the other efforts that the Police together with stakeholders are implementing to prevent the scourge of scams from further impacting our community and society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ScamShield largely performs the function of crowdsourcing so that we know what are the reported scam numbers and scam messages that the Police would verify backend and then, block.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we have to look at the use of ScamShield together with all these other channels that we are using to prevent the scourge of scams from further impacting our community.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the point of malware, the Member would note that in recent times, the major retail banks have already rolled out anti-malware applications via the digital banking apps.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Cyber Security Agency (CSA) has also shared a list of anti-malware security apps that members of the public could download on their own.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we need to consider, apart from the ScamShield app, all these other initiatives that would be helpful to the public in preventing scams from further impacting society.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
text: So, to this point, would the Minister of State consider looking at a potential upgrade of ScamShield?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
text: And secondly, would the Minister of State consider further upgrades to ScamShield if further monitoring of existing initiatives do not work out as well?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I shared in my main reply that, indeed, the GovTech team, specifically, is working on improving the ScamShield app.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The current area that they are looking to improve is to increase the value proposition of the ScamShield app to users.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The reason for that is because currently, ScamShield does not actively inform the user how many calls and SMSes have been blocked.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, that is something that the GovTech team is working on.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These are the areas that the GovTech team is working on.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We feel that it is through improvements in the features, functionality and the user experience of the app which would be key to enhancing the app's download rate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the point of malware, indeed, we are not just relying on the actions of the banks, we are not just relying on the digital banking apps of the banks to prevent malware.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, I am aware that there could be mobile users who, unfortunately, download malware unsuspectingly, for instance, when they click on links that are tainted APK files, for instance.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: From the perspective of cyber hygiene, this is something that the CSA is working on actively on the ground, together with digital ambassadors and the Infocomms Media Development Authority, to encourage better cyber hygiene practices, so that our members of society do not unwittingly download malware.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We also promote messages such as ensuring that any downloads of apps should be done from the official App Store or Google Play Store, for instance.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I do not think we should see the use of the ScamShield app as the only channel and the only app that would prevent our members of society from becoming victims of scams.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I would urge all of us to look at the suite of measures in its totality.
